subject: DPA exhibit: consent routing, SCC fallback and procurement path
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@vistacare.com>, Matthew Ortiz <matthew.ortiz@vistacare.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA exhibit: initial ask + attachments

Hi Samantha / Matthew —

Thanks again for taking time today. Per our call, attaching the draft DPA exhibit and an SCCs mapping table so your legal/procurement teams can see the callouts we expect to land. The main open items we flagged were:

- Customer consent routing (VistaCare wants EU-only processing unless explicit patient opt-in is provided)
- SCCs fallback approach if standard EU annex cannot be used for subprocessor chains
- Role split (controller vs processor responsibilities in order form exhibit)
- Procurement timing for signature + any DocuSign routing constraints

Short asks from your side: please confirm whether VistaCare requires us to carve out model training/derivative data, and whether you need an SLA exception for cross-border KV cache replication.

Attachments: dpa-exhibit_v1.pdf; sccs-mapping-table.xlsx

Next steps: Olga and Laura from our privacy team are looped on this thread — they'll provide redline guidance and an alternate fallback path for SCCs. Would you be able to confirm a preferred signatory and procurement timeline this week?

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

[Attachment stubs: dpa-exhibit_v1.pdf (PDF, 92KB), sccs-mapping-table.xlsx (XLSX, 28KB)]

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@vistacare.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Matthew Ortiz <matthew.ortiz@vistacare.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA exhibit: initial ask + attachments

Ben —

Appreciate the materials. Quick responses inline:

- Consent routing: VistaCare policy is EU residency by default for patient data. We can provide opt-in for model improvements but need the DPA to reflect explicit opt-in flow and an audit trail for each patient consent.
- SCCs: we cannot accept unilateral fallback language. If you need to rely on SCCs for subprocessors in non-EEA jurisdictions, we require a specific exception path and evidence of equivalent safeguards (e.g., contractual flow-down + technical guardrails).
- Role split: we will push back on any language that suggests VistaCare is a processor for any element of patient-identifiable data — we see Redwood as processor in the sense of serving inference, but the order form must make clear VistaCare is controller for patient record ingestion.
- Procurement: target signature next week (May 10). Procurement will own DocuSign routing but we need the DPA finalized by EOD May 7 to meet that.

We will loop in our privacy engineering contact if technical evidence is required for KV caching or replication patterns.

Samantha Lee
General Counsel, VistaCare Health
samantha.lee@vistacare.com

[Attached: none]

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@vistacare.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA exhibit: initial ask + attachments

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the clarity, that helps. Quick notes from Redwood legal/privacy:

1) Consent routing: we can add explicit consent scaffolding into the exhibit that requires a documented opt-in to allow processing outside the EU for model improvement purposes. We'll add a change log clause that preserves audit records for 2 years.

2) SCCs fallback: proposed approach (high level):
- Primary: standard SCCs (EU Commission clauses) for EEA -> non-EEA transfers when permitted.
- Fallback: when SCCs aren't sufficient (e.g., local law prevents application), Redwood will provide: (a) contractual flow-down to subprocessors, (b) technical mitigations (encryption at rest + strict egress controls), and (c) optional on-premises private deployment as a paid fallback.

Samantha, we can mark the fallback as "subject to mutual written approval" and include a defined evidence packet to be delivered within 5 business days of request. That gives you auditability while preserving operational options.

3) Role split: propose explicit clause in the order form exhibit: "Customer (VistaCare) is controller for Customer Data; Redwood is processor for the provision of inference services. Processor obligations do not convert controller responsibilities."

4) Action items / timeline:
- I will push a redline by EOD May 4 (dpa-exhibit_v2.docx).
- Ben: confirm whether sales are comfortable with the paid private-deploy fallback as one of the remedies.
- Samantha / Matthew: please confirm whether VistaCare will accept the evidence packet approach for SCCs fallback (we'll include the list of artifacts in the redline).

We'll keep procurement timing in mind — if we hit May 7 redline freeze, we can route for signature on May 10.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

[Planned attachments: redlines_dpa_v2.docx]

Thanks — brief procurement confirmation: VistaCare accepts the proposed timeline. A couple items on our end: 

- We will expect the evidence packet to include a clear list (SCCs mapping, subprocessors list with locations, encryption details, and contact for on-call security review).
- For the private-deploy fallback, procurement will need a SOW addendum with pricing bands and estimated turnaround times; please include draft numbers in the May 4 redline if possible.
- DocuSign routing: signatory will be Samantha Lee (GC) then CFO on our side. We'll provide the CFO email by EOD tomorrow.

If Olga's team can deliver v2 redline with the evidence artifacts called out, procurement will prep the DocuSign route.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Matthew Ortiz
Procurement Lead, VistaCare Health
